AbstractText.Label: BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE
AbstractText.content: Diabetic subjects with non-healing ulcers have a reduced expression of vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF). Genetically diabetic mice have an altered expression pattern of VEGF and its receptor, VEGFR-2. In diabetic wounds, miR15b and miR200b which respectively inhibit VEGF and VEGF-R2 mRNAs are up-regulated, further affecting the impaired angiogenesis. We investigated whether anti-miRs directed toward miR15b and miR200b could improve wound repair in genetically diabetic mice.

AbstractText.Label: EXPERIMENTAL APPROACH
AbstractText.content: Wounds were produced on the back skin of female diabetic mice, animals received in the wound edge, the anti-miRs (antimiR15b, antimiR200b, or antimiR15b/200b) at the dose of 10mg/Kg, or vehicle. Mice were killed on day 7, 14 and at time of complete wound closure.

AbstractText.Label: KEY RESULTS
AbstractText.content: mRNA expression of VEGF, VEGFR-2, Angiopoietin-1, and its receptor TEK were evaluated after 7 and 14 days. Protein levels of VEGF and transglutaminase II were measured at day 7, while VEGFR-2 and Angiopoietin-1 at day 14. Histological features and the time to achieve a complete wound closure were also examined. Treatment with the anti-miRs improved the analyzed parameters and the co-treatment resulted the most effective.

AbstractText.Label: CONCLUSION AND IMPLICATIONS
AbstractText.content: The results suggest that the inhibition of miR15b and miR200b may have a potential application in diabetes-related wound disorders.
